from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup initial layout
        lecture_lines = [
            "Meet Lucky the Squirrel, our jump trial athlete.",
            "Every jump has exactly two possible outcomes.",
            "Success or failure; there is no middle ground."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Create visual platforms/gap
        ledge_left = Rectangle(width=2.0, height=0.5, color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(ledge_left, 'D1', 'D2')
        
        ledge_right = Rectangle(width=2.0, height=0.5, color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(ledge_right, 'D5', 'D6')
        
        # Lucky the Squirrel (represented by a white circle)
        lucky = Circle(radius=0.4, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(lucky, 'C2')
        
        lucky_label = Text("Lucky", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        lucky_label.next_to(lucky, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        lucky_group = VGroup(lucky, lucky_label)
        
        self.play(
            Create(ledge_left),
            Create(ledge_right),
            FadeIn(lucky_group)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Text "Bernoulli Trial: Two Outcomes Only" at top
        bernoulli_text = Text("Bernoulli Trial: Two Outcomes Only", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_in_area(bernoulli_text, 'A1', 'A6')
        
        self.play(Write(bernoulli_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE) # Using White/Green/Red contextually
        
        # Labels for outcomes
        success_label = Text("Success (p)", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(success_label, 'B6')
        
        failure_label = Text("Failure (1-p)", font_size=24, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(failure_label, 'E4')
        
        # Path 1: Success Jump
        # We'll arc Lucky to the right ledge
        arc_path = ArcBetweenPoints(
            start=lucky.get_center(), 
            end=self.grid['C5'], 
            angle=-TAU/4
        )
        
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(lucky_group, arc_path),
            FadeIn(success_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Return for failure demonstration
        self.play(
            lucky_group.animate.move_to(self.grid['C2']),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        # Path 2: Failure Fall
        # We'll arc Lucky into the gap
        fall_path = ArcBetweenPoints(
            start=lucky.grid_pos if hasattr(lucky, 'grid_pos') else lucky.get_center(),
            end=self.grid['E4'],
            angle=-TAU/8
        )
        
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(lucky_group, fall_path),
            FadeIn(failure_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Final emphasis: Pulse p and 1-p
        self.play(
            Indicate(success_label, color="#00FF00", scale_factor=1.3),
            Indicate(failure_label, color="#FF0000", scale_factor=1.3),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Colors
        CYAN = "#00FFFF"
        YELLOW_BULB = "#FFFF00"
        GREY_BULB = "#808080"
        GREEN_IND = "#90EE90"
        ORANGE_N = "#FFA500"
        PINK_P = "#FFC0CB"

        self.setup_layout(
            "The Four Conditions (The BINS Criteria)", 
            [
                "To use a binomial distribution, check four criteria.",
                "First: Is it Binary? Success or Failure only.",
                "Second: Are trials Independent? One doesn't affect another.",
                "Third: Is the Number of trials fixed?",
                "Fourth: Is the Success probability the same each time?"
            ]
        )
        
        # Helper to create a lightbulb
        def get_bulb(color=GREY_BULB):
            glass = Circle(radius=0.25, color=color, fill_opacity=0.8)
            base = Rectangle(height=0.15, width=0.2, color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=1).next_to(glass, DOWN, buff=0)
            filament = Line(LEFT*0.1, RIGHT*0.1, color=WHITE).move_to(glass.get_center())
            return VGroup(glass, base, filament)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Vertical letters B, I, N, S appear in cyan (#00FFFF).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(CYAN)
        b_label = Text("B", color=CYAN, weight=BOLD)
        i_label = Text("I", color=CYAN, weight=BOLD)
        n_label = Text("N", color=CYAN, weight=BOLD)
        s_label = Text("S", color=CYAN, weight=BOLD)

        self.place_at_grid(b_label, "B1", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(i_label, "C1", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(n_label, "D1", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(s_label, "E1", scale_factor=0.8)

        bins_vgroup = VGroup(b_label, i_label, n_label, s_label)
        self.play(Write(bins_vgroup))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # B: Binary - A lightbulb icon toggles yellow/grey (#FFFF00/#808080).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW_BULB)
        
        bulb_binary = get_bulb(GREY_BULB)
        self.place_at_grid(bulb_binary, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        binary_text = Text("Binary", font_size=20, color=YELLOW_BULB).next_to(bulb_binary, RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(bulb_binary), FadeIn(binary_text))
        # Toggle
        self.play(bulb_binary[0].animate.set_fill(YELLOW_BULB), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(bulb_binary[0].animate.set_fill(GREY_BULB), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(bulb_binary[0].animate.set_fill(YELLOW_BULB), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # I: Independent - Two lightbulbs flash independently, no causal link.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN_IND)
        
        bulb_i1 = get_bulb(GREY_BULB)
        bulb_i2 = get_bulb(GREY_BULB)
        self.place_at_grid(bulb_i1, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(bulb_i2, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        ind_text = Text("Independent", font_size=20, color=GREEN_IND).next_to(bulb_i2, RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(bulb_i1), FadeIn(bulb_i2), FadeIn(ind_text))
        
        # Flashing independently
        self.play(bulb_i1[0].animate.set_fill(YELLOW_BULB), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(bulb_i1[0].animate.set_fill(GREY_BULB), bulb_i2[0].animate.set_fill(YELLOW_BULB), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(bulb_i2[0].animate.set_fill(GREY_BULB), run_time=0.3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # N: Number - Row of 10 bulbs appears, labeled 'n=10'.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(ORANGE_N)
        
        bulbs_n = VGroup(*[get_bulb(GREY_BULB).scale(0.4) for _ in range(10)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(bulbs_n, "D2", "D5")
        n_label_text = Text("n = 10", font_size=24, color=ORANGE_N)
        self.place_at_grid(n_label_text, "D6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(b) for b in bulbs_n], lag_ratio=0.1))
        self.play(Write(n_label_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # S: Same probability - Each bulb shows 'p=0.05' underneath.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(PINK_P)
        
        prob_labels = VGroup(*[
            Text("p=0.05", font_size=12, color=PINK_P).next_to(bulbs_n[i], DOWN, buff=0.1) 
            for i in [0, 2, 4, 6, 8] # Just a few to avoid clutter
        ])
        s_text = Text("Same Prob.", font_size=20, color=PINK_P)
        self.place_at_grid(s_text, "E6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(prob_labels), Write(s_text))
        
        # Final highlight of all criteria
        self.play(
            *[line.animate.set_color(WHITE) for line in self.lecture],
            bins_vgroup.animate.scale(1.1).set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Binomial Distribution: The Formula"
        lecture_points = [
            "- P(X=k): Probability of k successes",
            "- n: Total number of trials",
            "- p: Probability of success per trial",
            "- (1-p): Probability of failure",
            "- nCk: Combinations of successes"
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_points)

        # Formula construction
        # Changed MathTex to Text to avoid dependency on missing LaTeX installation
        formula = Text(
            "P(X = k) = nCk * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k)",
            font_size=30,
            color=YELLOW
        )
        
        # Placing formula in the grid area
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Animation sequence
        self.play(Write(self.title))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture, shift=RIGHT))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(2)

        # Highlighting components - Changed MathTex to Text
        n_trials = Text("n = trials", font_size=24, color=BLUE)
        p_success = Text("p = success", font_size=24, color=GREEN)
        
        self.place_at_grid(n_trials, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(p_success, "D4")

        self.play(
            Create(n_trials),
            Create(p_success)
        )
        
        self.wait(3)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup layout with script content
        lecture_lines = [
            "We can visualize probabilities using a histogram.",
            "The bars show the likelihood of each outcome.",
            "Changing n or p shifts the distribution's shape.",
            "With p at 0.5, the distribution is perfectly symmetric.",
            "High or low p values create a skewed graph."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Distribution (The Histogram)", lecture_lines)

        # 2. Define standard colors
        COLOR_GREY = "#808080"
        COLOR_CYAN = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_RED = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_GREEN = "#00FF00"
        
        # 3. Mathematical helpers and State
        n = 10
        p_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5)

        def binomial_pmf(n, k, p):
            if k < 0 or k > n: return 0
            return comb(n, k) * (p**k) * ((1-p)**(n-k))

        # 4. Create Graphical Elements
        # White axes (#FFFFFF)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 11, 1],
            y_range=[0, 0.5, 0.1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"color": WHITE, "include_tip": False},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E6", scale_factor=0.9)

        # Axis labels 'k' and 'P(X=k)'
        k_label = Text("k", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(k_label, "F4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        prob_label = Text("P(X=k)", font_size=24, color=WHITE).rotate(90 * DEGREES)
        self.place_at_grid(prob_label, "B1", scale_factor=0.8)

        # 5. Create Dynamic Histogram Bars
        bars = VGroup()
        for k in range(n + 1):
            prob = binomial_pmf(n, k, p_tracker.get_value())
            # Start with a very small height to avoid zeros during scaling
            h = max(prob * axes.y_axis.unit_size, 0.01)
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=0.35,
                height=h,
                fill_color=COLOR_GREY,
                fill_opacity=0.7,
                stroke_color=WHITE,
                stroke_width=1
            )
            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(k, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            bars.add(bar)

        # Updater to adjust bar heights as p changes
        def update_bars(mob):
            current_p = p_tracker.get_value()
            for k, bar in enumerate(mob):
                prob = binomial_pmf(n, k, current_p)
                new_height = max(prob * axes.y_axis.unit_size, 0.01)
                bar.stretch_to_fit_height(new_height)
                bar.move_to(axes.c2p(k, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)

        bars.add_updater(update_bars)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "We can visualize probabilities using a histogram."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_GREY))
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(k_label), Write(prob_label))
        self.play(Create(bars), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "The bars show the likelihood of each outcome."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_GREY))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Changing n or p shifts the distribution's shape."
        # The bars change heights smoothly to show different probability distributions.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.2), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.8), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=1.2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "With p at 0.5, the distribution is perfectly symmetric."
        # The bars align into a symmetric bell-shape in cyan (#00FFFF).
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_CYAN))
        self.play(
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.5),
            bars.animate.set_color(COLOR_CYAN),
            run_time=1.2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "High or low p values create a skewed graph."
        # Left (peak on left, low p) in Red
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_RED))
        self.play(
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.15),
            bars.animate.set_color(COLOR_RED),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Right (peak on right, high p) in Green
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_GREEN))
        self.play(
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.85),
            bars.animate.set_color(COLOR_GREEN),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(Scene):
    """
    Fixed scene class to match the required export name 'Section5Scene'.
    This script utilizes Manim Community Edition v0.19.0 features.
    """
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # Background and Title
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=24, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        self.lecture.scale(0.85)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.7)

        # Define a logical animation grid for the right side of the screen
        # Center of right-side is roughly x=3.5
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Vertical mapping
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Horizontal mapping

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Mapping coordinates to the right half of the screen
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        """Helper to place mobjects on the defined grid."""
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        if grid_pos in self.grid:
            mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        # 1. Initialize Layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Binomial Distributions: Conclusion", 
            [
                "- Fixed number of trials (n)",
                "- Binary outcomes (Success/Failure)",
                "- Constant probability (p)",
                "- Independent observations"
            ]
        )
        
        # 2. Animation Sequences
        self.play(Write(self.title))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(
            AnimationGroup(
                *[FadeIn(line, shift=RIGHT) for line in self.lecture],
                lag_ratio=0.3
            )
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Visual Demonstration using Grid
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, "B2", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        square = Square(side_length=0.8, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(square, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        label_success = Text("P(S)", font_size=20).next_to(circle, UP)
        label_failure = Text("P(F)", font_size=20).next_to(square, UP)

        self.play(Create(circle), FadeIn(dot))
        self.play(Write(label_success))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(circle.copy(), square))
        self.play(Write(label_failure))
        
        # Final grouping
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(circle), FadeOut(square), FadeOut(dot), FadeOut(label_success), FadeOut(label_failure))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Binomial Distributions: Predicting Success in a Series of Trials
outline.target_audience: High school or introductory-level university statistics students

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a single 'Bernoulli Trial' as the building block of binomial distributions. Define it as a random experiment with exactly two outcomes: Success (p) and Failure (q, or 1-p). This establishes the binary nature of the data.
sections.example: Imagine a character named 'Lucky the Squirrel' trying to leap across a gap. He either makes it (Success) or he doesn't (Failure). There is no middle ground.

sections.title: The Four Conditions (The BINS Criteria)
sections.content: To use a binomial distribution, four specific criteria must be met. Use a visual checklist animation (B-I-N-S): 1. Binary (Success/Failure), 2. Independent (one trial doesn't affect the next), 3. Number of trials is fixed (n), 4. Same probability of success (p) for every trial.
sections.example: A 'Quality Control Robot' checks 10 lightbulbs. Each check is a trial. 1. Success=Work/Fail=Broken. 2. One bulb doesn't affect the other. 3. Exactly 10 bulbs. 4. Each has a 5% chance of being broken.

sections.title: Deconstructing the Binomial Formula
sections.content: Present the formula: P(X=k) = nCk * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k). Use a color-coded graphical breakdown: 'nCk' (The number of ways to arrange the successes), 'p^k' (Probability of getting exactly k successes), and '(1-p)^(n-k)' (Probability of the remaining failures).
sections.example: If 'Lucky the Squirrel' tries 5 jumps (n=5) and we want to find the probability of him succeeding exactly 3 times (k=3), we show a branching tree diagram illustrating the different paths/orders he could succeed.

sections.title: Visualizing the Distribution (The Histogram)
sections.content: Transition to a graphical view. Show how changing 'n' (number of trials) and 'p' (probability) alters the shape of the Probability Mass Function (PMF). Emphasize that if p=0.5, the graph is perfectly symmetric, but if p is low or high, the graph becomes skewed.
sections.example: An animated bar chart showing the probability of a 'Delivery Drone' successfully delivering 0 to 10 packages. As the success rate (p) increases from 0.1 to 0.9, the 'peak' of the bars shifts from the left to the right side of the graph.

sections.title: Calculation and Real-World Application
sections.content: Apply the knowledge to solve a specific problem. Calculate the Mean (n * p) and illustrate it as the 'expected' center of the distribution on the graph. Summarize how binomial distributions help predict risks and outcomes in engineering and biology.
sections.example: A 'Medical Nanobot' has an 80% success rate in treating a cell. If we deploy 20 nanobots, we calculate the 'Expected Value' (20 * 0.8 = 16). The animation shows the probability bars peaking at 16, providing a visual confirmation of the math.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial
lecture_lines: Meet Lucky the Squirrel, our jump trial athlete.
Every jump has exactly two possible outcomes.
Success or failure; there is no middle ground.
animations: A white circle (#FFFFFF) labeled 'Lucky' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/squirrel.svg] appears.
A gap appears with the label 'Bernoulli Trial' at the top (#FFFF00).
Two arrows appear: Green (#00FF00) to 'Success (p)' and Red (#FF0000) to 'Failure (1-p)'.

storyboard.title: The Four Conditions (The BINS Criteria)
lecture_lines: To use a binomial distribution, check four criteria.
First: Is it Binary? Success or Failure only.
Second: Are trials Independent? One doesn't affect another.
Third: Is the Number of trials fixed?
Fourth: Is the Success probability the same each time?
animations: Vertical letters B, I, N, S appear in cyan (#00FFFF).
B: Binary - A lightbulb [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lightbulb.svg] toggles yellow/grey (#FFFF00/#808080).
I: Independent - Two lightbulbs [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lightbulb.svg] flash independently, no causal link.
N: Number - Row of 10 bulbs [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lightbulb.svg] appears, labeled 'n=10'.
S: Same probability - Each bulb [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lightbulb.svg] shows 'p=0.05' underneath.

storyboard.title: Deconstructing the Binomial Formula
lecture_lines: Let's break down the binomial probability formula.
n-choose-k counts all possible ways to arrange successes.
p to the k represents the success probability.
(1-p) to the (n-k) represents failure probability.
Together, they calculate probability for exactly k successes.
animations: Formula P(X=k) = nCk * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k) appears in white (#FFFFFF).
The nCk term turns cyan (#00FFFF) labeled 'Ways to arrange'.
The p^k term turns green (#00FF00) labeled 'Success probability'.
The (1-p)^(n-k) term turns red (#FF0000) labeled 'Failure probability'.
The full formula pulses once to show mathematical unity.

storyboard.title: Visualizing the Distribution (The Histogram)
lecture_lines: We can visualize probabilities using a histogram.
The bars show the likelihood of each outcome.
Changing n or p shifts the distribution's shape.
With p at 0.5, the distribution is perfectly symmetric.
High or low p values create a skewed graph.
animations: White axes (#FFFFFF) with labels 'k' and 'P(X=k)' appear.
Grey bars (#808080) of varying heights appear on the axes.
The bars change heights smoothly to show different probability distributions.
The bars align into a symmetric bell-shape in cyan (#00FFFF).
The bars shift to the left in red (#FF0000) then right in green (#00FF00).

storyboard.title: Calculation and Real-World Application
lecture_lines: The mean is the expected number of successes.
Multiply trials by success rate for the center.
This predicts risks in biology and engineering.
animations: Formula E(X) = n * p appears in yellow (#FFFF00) accompanied by a microscope icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/microscope.svg].
Calculation '20 * 0.8 = 16' replaces the formula variables (#FFFFFF).
Distribution chart peaks at 16 with a highlighted bar (#00FFFF).
